question: Which type of genital fistula accounts for the majority of obstetric fistulae in low-resource settings, and what is the primary anatomical communication it creates?

answers.text: Recto-vaginal fistula — between the rectum and the vagina

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Recto-vaginal fistula (RVF) does occur in obstetric contexts (especially with fourth-degree tear breakdown) but is far less common than VVF. VVF is the most prevalent obstetric fistula.

answers.text: Vesico-vaginal fistula — between the urinary bladder and the vagina

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Vesico-vaginal fistula (VVF) is by far the most common obstetric fistula globally, accounting for approximately 85–90% of cases. It forms between the posterior wall of the bladder and the anterior vaginal wall, typically after prolonged obstructed labour causes ischaemic necrosis of the intervening tissue.

answers.text: Uretero-vaginal fistula — between the ureter and the vagina

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Uretero-vaginal fistula (UVF) is predominantly iatrogenic (from gynaecological surgery, especially hysterectomy) rather than obstetric. It presents with continuous leakage but with some preserved bladder voiding, which distinguishes it clinically from VVF.

answers.text: Vesico-uterine fistula — between the bladder and the uterus

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Vesico-uterine fistula is rare and more commonly follows caesarean section (especially repeat CS) rather than obstructed vaginal delivery. The classic presentation is cyclical haematuria (Youssef syndrome), not continuous urine loss.

overallFeedback.feedback: VVF (bladder-to-vagina) is the most common obstetric fistula (~85–90%). UVF is usually surgical/iatrogenic. Vesico-uterine fistula follows CS. RVF can follow 4th-degree tear breakdown.
Correct. VVF is the most prevalent obstetric fistula; the key cause in low-resource settings is prolonged obstructed labour causing ischaemic necrosis.
